title: Provider migration
description: Controlled replacement of the provider behind one or more capabilities (ADR-BCP-006 sections 44-58, 119-120, Gate 8). Capability keys and canonical contracts never change: only which provider serves them, cohort by cohort. A migration is planned side-effect free, as a ChangePlan (change-plan.schema.json) whose steps are canonical migration operations; the Control Plane never assumes that routing alone moves business state (section 53) and never introduces dual authoritative writers (sections 55-56). Stages are in provider-migration-lifecycle.yaml. A definition library; validate against #/$defs/ProviderMigrationRequest, #/$defs/ProviderMigrationPlan or #/$defs/ProviderMigration.

migrationStage.description: ADR-BCP-006 section 45, plus the two ways a migration ends without completing. Section 45's DISCOVER is the side-effect-free preview (POST /provider-migrations/plan), never a stage a migration is in: a migration is created in PLAN, already discovered. COMPLETE, CANCELLED and ROLLED_BACK are terminal. Transitions are in provider-migration-lifecycle.yaml.

migrationMode.description: Section 54. STATELESS_REBIND: the capabilities hold no business state the source owns, so moving bindings migrates them. STATEFUL_CUTOVER: the source is a system of record for mutable state; exactly one provider stays authoritative at every moment (section 55), and the data strategy moves the state before each cohort's authority moves.

dataStrategy.description: How business state reaches the target before authority moves. NONE only for STATELESS_REBIND, and required there. Both cutover strategies end with a write freeze on the cohort, reconciliation and post-cutover verification (section 54). Dual write is deliberately absent: it needs its own architecture decision (section 56).

rollbackStrategy.description: How a cohort returns to the source. REBIND_SOURCE: bindings move back; valid when the source still holds authoritative state. RESTORE_AND_REBIND_SOURCE: state written to the target after cutover is migrated back first. FORWARD_FIX_ONLY: no return; the plan warns MIGRATION_NOT_REVERSIBLE and its risk class is at least HIGH.

contract_version.description: The capability contract major version the migrated bindings require (binding.schema.json required_contract_version). The target must support it before it may receive authoritative traffic (section 48).

cohortSelector.description: A deterministic set of contexts (section 51): dimensions combine with AND, values within a dimension with OR. Never a percentage: percentage rollout needs a formal traffic policy this contract does not define (sections 51-52).

migrationCohort.description: One step of the rollout, in order. The first cohort is the canary (section 50). Exactly one cohort, the last, may omit its selector: it takes every affected context the earlier cohorts did not.

ProviderMigrationRequest.description: What an operator asks to migrate (section 120). The same body previews a plan (POST /provider-migrations/plan, side-effect free) and creates the migration (POST /provider-migrations). Everything else a plan needs (affected bindings, tenants, estates, markets, contract compatibility, target readiness) the Control Plane discovers from authoritative state (section 46); the request never supplies it.

target_provider_key.description: Must differ from source_provider_key: moving a provider's own instances is an engine upgrade or instance replacement (sections 59-60), not a provider migration.

shadow.description: Request a SHADOW stage (section 49). The Control Plane refuses shadow for capabilities whose operations mutate state unless the provider declares them shadow-safe (MIGRATION_SHADOW_UNSAFE); shadow never determines a result (section 41).

validation_checks.description: Operator-specified checks each cohort must pass in VALIDATE, beyond the checks the Control Plane always adds.

owners.description: Canonical principals accountable for the migration (section 120). Never emails.

migrationOperation.description: Canonical, Baobab-native migration operations. Provider-specific work is a resolved resource of a step, never its type. A STATEFUL_CUTOVER cohort always runs FREEZE_COHORT_WRITES, MIGRATE_COHORT_DATA, RECONCILE_COHORT_DATA, SHIFT_COHORT, UNFREEZE_COHORT_WRITES in that order, so authority never has two holders. CREATE_MIGRATION_BINDING is one step per capability and target instance, naming exactly the source bindings that move to that instance. REMOVE_MIGRATION_BINDING is compensation only (cancel and roll_back, provider-migration-lifecycle.yaml compensation and rollback_steps) and never appears in a plan.

migrationStepResources.description: The resolved resources a step acts on, in ADR-SHARED-012 identifiers.

binding_ids.description: The source bindings the step acts on. A CREATE_MIGRATION_BINDING step names them with the one target engine_instance_id they move to, so the approved plan fixes every binding's target instance and nothing is re-resolved after approval.

migrationDiscovery.description: What the migration touches, discovered from authoritative state (section 46). Every affected context belongs to exactly one cohort; a context no cohort takes is the blocker MIGRATION_CONTEXT_UNASSIGNED.

ProviderMigrationPlan.description: The immutable migration plan (sections 47, 120, 123): a ChangePlan whose steps are canonical migration operations and whose blockers include every unmet precondition of section 48 (see provider-migration-lifecycle.yaml blocking_codes). It embeds the request it was planned from, so the reviewed artifact is the whole intent. source_provider_key, target_provider_key and migration_mode repeat the request's for readers and must equal them. A previewed plan has no provider_migration_id; a created migration's plan does.

request.description: The complete intent the plan executes: capabilities, cohorts, data, rollback and shadow strategy, cutover window, validation checks and owners. Part of the plan's material, so an approval bound to the digest covers all of it.

migrationTransition.description: A command transition of provider-migration-lifecycle.yaml. Which plan operations each runs is its stage_steps (ADR-SHARED-016 section 2).

ProviderMigrationAdvanceRequest.description: Advance the migration by one transition. Forward transitions need an APPROVED decision on the current, unblocked, unexpired, non-stale plan, no running operation of the migration, and, for canary and shift, an open cutover window where one is named; cancel and roll_back need no approval. The Control Plane derives the steps from the approved plan; a request never names them.

ProviderMigration.description: The migration aggregate (section 119). Created in PLAN with its first plan. Advancing past PLAN is a controlled mutation (ADR-BCP-021): an approval binds to the plan digest, and stages execute as durable operations (ADR-BCP-022). Execution: one approval binds the plan, and each stage is an explicit advance (ADR-SHARED-016).

current_cohort_key.description: The cohort in CANARY or SHIFT, or being validated.

blocked.description: The current plan has blockers; the migration cannot advance until a new plan clears them.

approval_id.description: The APPROVED decision on the current plan's digest, once approved (ADR-SHARED-016 section 1). Absent before approval and after a replan.

operation_id.description: The latest PROVIDER_MIGRATION_ADVANCE operation. A migration runs one operation at a time.

shifted_cohort_keys.description: Cohorts whose authority has moved to the target, in order. Rollback returns them most recent first (ADR-SHARED-016 section 5).
